fixes.explanation: One talent is what the third servant was handed, so that's a different man. The five-talent servant is the one in this verse. The text says he gained five more. That's a full doubling, and he got there by putting the money to work.
Verse 18 says he “…dug a hole in the ground, and hid his master’s money.” That's it. That's the whole plan. The other two servants were out putting the money to work, and he was out digging a hole.

The passage never says he gave anything to anybody. Verse 18 says he “…dug a hole in the ground, and hid his master’s money.” Hiding it is what the text says he did. I think a hole in the ground is a lonely place for a talent.
He doesn't say angry. Verse 25 has him saying, “So I was afraid and went out and hid your talent in the ground.” He doesn't mention anger at all. The word he gives the master is afraid.

Giving to the poor isn't what the master says here. He says the servant “…should have deposited my money with the bankers…” The money was the master's, and he says what to do with it. The bankers are the answer, and the interest would have come with them.

The master doesn't name a steward here. He names the receiver by his count: “…the one who has ten talents.” That's the first servant, the one who put his five to work and gained five more. Verse 28 has the master say it plainly.

The text doesn't send the servant to a far country. Verse 30 says he is thrown “…into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.” I think this is a heavy verse, so let's take it as it is.
